predictions.title: Indirect prompt injection becomes a top CVE category by Q3 2026
predictions.body: Indirect prompt injection has already crossed from one-off advisory curiosity into a recognized CVE category, roughly six weeks ahead of the Q3 2026 window the prediction first named. The May 16 bridge (validation.e29cec4d9bd15d9b, support 'because') catalogues eleven tooling-stack instances under a Trail of Bits four-tier taxonomy, with a CISA federal-civilian directive queued behind them -- the markers of a category, not a curiosity. Successful indirect-prompt-injection attacks are up +190% YoY, and CVE-2025-53773-style RCE-from-PR-body flaws reproduce trivially because LLM coding assistants and agentic tools read untrusted text -- PRs, issues, web pages -- straight into privileged execution paths. The open question is no longer whether the category appears but whether it sticks: the forward test is a sustained Patch Tuesday cadence of CVSS 8.0+ LLM-integration CVEs through Q3 2026, not a single first occurrence.

reasoning.plain_language: AI tools run hidden commands from things they read. This bug type is now recognized, six weeks early. Will monthly patches keep coming?
